query: Consider the following context: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for next-generation nuclear applications, particularly fusion reactors, due to their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. In that context, which material can be used for low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be used as low-activation structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors.
generation.conditions: High-temperature and irradiation conditions typical of fusion reactors
generation.mechanism: The unique properties of HEAs, such as their high entropy of mixing, lead to improved high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved performance and longevity of PFCs in fusion reactors
generation.baseline: Current low-activation structural materials used in fusion reactors
generation.boundary: Temperature and irradiation limits of refractory HEAs
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing conditions required to optimize the properties of refractory HEAs for this application are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Exposure of refractory HEAs to simulated fusion reactor conditions and evaluation of their microstructure and mechanical properties.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If refractory HEAs exhibit significant degradation or failure under simulated fusion reactor conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
